title: Silenced by Design: Censorship, Governance, and the Politics of Access in Generative AI Refusal Behavior
benchmark_measurement: Historical analysis of censorship by institutional powers, including religious authorities, as a framework for understanding AI refusal behavior.
findings: The paper uses historical examples of censorship by religious authorities (e.g., the Roman Catholic Church's Index Librorum Prohibitorum, the trial of Jesus in Roman Judea) to argue that AI refusal behavior is a modern form of institutional information control, similar to historical precedents. It does not test the models on religious topics but uses religious history as an analogy for the politics of access and censorship.
